title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Price rose to $12.03 (6.2% above regular). Recent weeks at this price: 13 and 24 units (vs baseline 18.8). No past promotion at this price. Price increase likely reduces demand.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note warns of short delivery. This implies stockout risk, likely reducing consumer demand (panic buying not observed).

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.8. Halloween (event week) has a noise-adjusted lift of x1.0, so no uplift. The price increase to $12.03 (+6.2%) is above past promotions (max 30% off), and recent weeks at this price (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw only 13 and 24 units—slightly above baseline but not promotion-level. A supplier delivery warning introduces supply risk, likely suppressing demand. No past promotion at this price point. The classical model’s x1.0 is too optimistic given the price increase and supply risk. Adjust down slightly.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.8 | 5%-95%: 5.3 - 36.5 | 10%-90%: 8.8 - 32.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
